root_cause.text: In vmwgfx KMS framebuffer creation, vmw_kms_fb_create() unconditionally called surface->res.func->dirty_alloc() for a surface even when surface->res.dirty was already initialized, overwriting the existing dirty-tracker pointer and leaking the previously allocated tracker.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes vmw_kms_fb_create() from always doing `ret = surface->res.func->dirty_alloc(&surface->res);` to only doing so under `if (surface->res.dirty == NULL)`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states “We were overwriting the surface's dirty tracker here causing a memory leak.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid reallocating a surface dirty tracker during framebuffer creation by only calling dirty_alloc when no dirty state exists.
intent_record.what: The code changes the unconditional call to surface->res.func->dirty_alloc(&surface->res) into a conditional call guarded by checking whether surface->res.dirty == NULL, while keeping the surrounding conditions and setting surface->res.coherent = true unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, dirty_alloc is now invoked only when the surface resource does not already have a dirty tracking object, preventing redundant or repeated dirty allocation for surfaces that were already initialized while still allocating it when missing.

grouping_result.intent: Avoid reallocating a surface dirty tracker during framebuffer creation by only calling dirty_alloc when no dirty state exists.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it prevents vmw_kms_fb_create() from calling dirty_alloc() when a surface already has dirty state, avoiding overwriting the existing tracker and leaking the previous allocation.

candidates.rationale: This is the direct cause of the bug: it allocates a new dirty tracker for the surface without checking whether surface->res.dirty is already initialized, overwriting the existing tracker pointer and leaking the prior allocation.

This guard is insufficient because it permits dirty_alloc whenever the callback exists, but does not verify that no dirty tracker is already present. That missing condition enables the unconditional reallocation.
